Printed white card

Choosing a white card folding carton for retail products

FORME Packaging editorialUpdated October 21, 20263 min read

White-card cartons provide a clean printed surface in a folded paperboard structure. The stock, crease, closure and product support all affect the finished result.

In this guideSpecify solid paperboard clearlyChoose the top and bottom constructionPlan artwork around the erected cartonApprove assembly and appearance togetherDiscuss your packaging →

Specify solid paperboard clearly

SBS is a white paperboard option used for printed folding cartons. Specify the proposed stock, coating and caliper with the supplier. Paper weight alone does not describe every aspect of stiffness or the way a folded pack will behave.

A genuine folding carton has thin solid-card cut edges and creased panels. It does not have the visible flute layers of corrugated board or the thick wrapped walls of a setup gift box. That distinction matters when reviewing samples, quotations and product imagery.

Choose the top and bottom construction

Straight-tuck and reverse-tuck cartons describe the relationship between the top and bottom opening panels. Other formats use lock bottoms or pre-glued bottom structures. The appropriate choice depends on the product, carton proportions and packing process.

Check the filled carton, particularly with bottles or candle jars. The bottom closure and internal support need to suit the weight. A decorative outer carton may also require separate protective shipping packaging.

Plan artwork around the erected carton

Reserve clear panels for the product name and essential information. Confirm the barcode position, opening direction, glue flap and safe distance from cuts and creases. Foil or embossing artwork should be reviewed against the chosen stock and the supplier’s process limits.

Windows and hanging headers add structural details. A window needs adequate surrounding board and an agreed patch material if enclosed. A hanging tab needs a properly located slot and a pack configuration suitable for the retail display.

Approve assembly and appearance together

  • Carton stands square and the side seam is clean.
  • Tuck flap closes without catching the dust flaps.
  • Product and insert fit without bowing the panels.
  • Print and finishing align with the intended panels.
  • Bottom closure and packed handling meet the brief.

Explore the white-card product series for skincare, perfume, tea, candles, electronics and confectionery applications.
